answer: The declaration is a juniper header, so 1939 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Fingerprints are counted in zephyr, and as a result the distribution is public, and karst lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 2 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
